## How to read this

This breakdown is derived from the five route treatments in `wiki/treatment/`
(Ember, Isolde, Seraphine, Wren, and the dark **Undivided** / polygamy arc) and
the shared act skeleton in `wiki/outline.md`.

**Branch model.** All five routes share one trunk: the opening act and the early
part of act two are the *same* scenes for everyone, coloured only by which love
interest Caedon gravitates toward. The story then forks:

```
COMMON TRUNK (Act I + early Act II)
        │
        ├─ c11_execution  ← the stranded-pair execution beat = the fork
        │
        ├── romance branches (determined by accumulated affection):
        │     ├─ EMBER   (em_*)
        │     ├─ ISOLDE  (is_*)
        │     ├─ SERAPHINE (se_*)
        │     └─ WREN    (wr_*)
        │
        └── DARK BRANCH: "The Undivided" (ud_*)
              — taken when Caedon has committed to NO single love interest;
                it diverges AT c11_execution and never rejoins.
```

The four romance branches reuse every trunk scene verbatim; they differ only in
their act-two tail and act three, and each ends in a wedding. The dark branch is
foreshadowed from Act I by *how* Caedon plays the trunk (cataloguing rather than
courting), but only formally splits off at the execution beat, and ends in
conquest + a timeskip civil war, no wedding.

**Scene IDs.** `c##_*` = common trunk. `em_/is_/se_/wr_/ud_*` = per-route. IDs
are stable handles for the eventual `[[scene: ...]]` markers and

I've now traced the whole structure, and the honest picture is different from the premise — so I want to check with you before proposing work, rather than split scenes in a way that would fight your own story bible.

## What I found

**The `[[line: Ln]]` / `[[nextline: N]]` markers are not errors.** They're a
machine-managed line-addressing scheme (in `opening.md` the file stores L1, L3, L2, L4 out of
order — the marker sets display order). All 40 scenes use them and validation reports **0 errors,
0 warnings**. I'll leave them alone.

**No scene file actually contains two scenes.** Every file has exactly one heading and one id;
every `next:`/`choice:` target resolves; the entry scene reaches everything. Structurally the
graph is sound.

**What you're seeing in c08 is "route colour," not packed branches.** c08 (and the same in
`c06_the_ruins`, `c07_the_ambush`, `c09_woods_training`, `c11b_on_the_run`, and
`c11_execution`) carries paragraphs literally labelled `(Ember path)`, `(Isolde path)`,
`(Seraphine path)`, `(Wren path)`, `(Undivided path)`. Per `wiki/breakdown_md.md`, this is the
**documented, intended design**:

> "All five routes share one trunk… the *same* scenes for everyone, coloured only by which love
> interest Caedon gravitates toward. The story then forks [at] `c11_execution`."
> "The four romance branches reuse every trunk scene verbatim."

So the single fork is `c11_execution` (correctly built with five `[[choice:]]` edges → the
`em_/is_/se_/wr_/ud_` routes). The `(… path)` paragraphs are meant to be shared-scene variants,
**not** separate scenes to split out.

**The one real defect** is that those variants are written as plain labelled prose with no
conditional mechanism (this marker set has no "show-if-route" line). So today every reader sees
all five paragraphs stacked in the same scene — which is exactly why c08 *reads* like branches
crammed together. That's a presentation problem, not a wiring problem.

## Why I'm not just splitting

Splitting c06–c09/c11b into per-route scenes would (a) directly contradict the "reuse every
trunk scene verbatim, single fork at c11_execution" model in your bible, (b) require a new
choice point earlier in Act I where the route is picked (there is none today — the trunk is all
linear `next:`), and (c) mean ~30 new scenes plus rewiring. That's a real design change, not a
cleanup, so I don't want to guess at it.

Here's how I'd like to proceed:
